g.text: GLINT
Current pipeline → Production design
31 October 2026 • Brackets explain each tool • Right-hand side is a proposed target, not a deployed system
TODAY — LOCAL APP
One computer runs the server; phone connects through a tunnel.
PRODUCTION — PROPOSED
A hosted service with reliable voice, user accounts and operations.
1 Phone / browser
React [screen] + browser camera and microphone
Silero [speech detection] • WeSpeaker [optional speaker check]
MediaPipe [body-position cues] • front/back camera switch
1 Phone / browser
Keep the same simple UI, local speech checks and camera controls.
Immediate stop [does not wait for the network]
Visible transcript, reconnect state and front/back camera switch
2 Local server
Node.js + Express [handle requests on your computer]
Cookie session [local user separation] • key stays in memory
Cloudflare quick tunnel [temporary public link to your computer]
2 Secure hosted entry
Stable HTTPS domain + streaming-capable proxy [secure connection]
Managed login [real user accounts] + session gateway [routing]
One session owner; bounded buffers; provider calls stay server-side
3 Understand speech and write the answer
Muse Voice Transcribe [live audio → recognized words]
Final words + recent images + conversation → Muse Spark
Muse Spark [understands context and streams answer text]
3 Dedicated voice path
Live ASR [speech → words] → turn coordinator [one user turn]
Fresh task context → Muse Spark [short, grounded streamed reply]
Request IDs [reject old results] • voice does not wait for vision
4 Generate spoken audio
Kokoro + sherpa-onnx [generate sentence audio on local CPU]
Device voice [fallback; Telugu depends on available phone voice]
Text can arrive well before audio; synthesis is a current bottleneck.
4 Qualified streaming speech
Speech engine [choose by measured speed + language support]
Generate small playable audio chunks; keep models warm.
Isolated speech worker [old / canceled jobs cannot block new voice]
5 Return to the user
SSE [web response streaming text and audio updates]
Web Audio [plays sound] • visible transcripts and captions
Microphone continues listening; local controls stop playback
5 Deliver and verify playback
Stream audio + text immediately through the gateway.
Browser reports first audio played [measure what the user hears].
Explicit language / device fallback; test Telugu + English on phones.
CAMERA PATH — runs beside conversation
Camera → up to 6 images from 8 seconds → Muse Spark → activity summary
Idle checks about every 6 seconds; questions also use recent frames.
No reliable persistent tracking of cups, tools or other task objects yet.
CAMERA PATH — separate background work
Useful frames → bounded vision worker [limited background processing]
Fresh evidence + task state → context used by the voice path
Optional SAM [object tracking] only after accuracy / cost / speed tests
MEMORY AND LIMITS
Session history + visual summary [temporary app memory]
SQLite [local file database]: optional progress, seven-day expiry
100 provider dispatches [request allowance]; no dollar spending cap
DATA AND OPERATIONS
PostgreSQL [durable task database] + per-user access checks
Consent-based media retention; optional private storage if needed
Spend controls, stage timings, alerts, deletion, load and device tests
WHAT CHANGES FOR PRODUCTION?
Keep the core: live speech → words + camera context → Spark → spoken reply.
Replace the temporary tunnel and shared local speech bottleneck with hosted, measured and isolated services.
Do not add every proposed tool at once: start with one gateway, a speech worker and a database; expand when measurements justify it.
Reality check: production performance is a target to prove. A native speech-to-speech API is not used by the current Meta pipeline.
Current timings in your logs: Spark text about 2–4 s; TTS generation / queue can take several seconds longer. These are examples, not benchmarks.
Drawing: editable SVG + Node.js; PNG rendered by Playwright / Chromium. Current side reflects code; production side is an architectural recommendation.
